items.definition:
to encourage something to grow, develop, or become active
The government introduced measures to stimulate the economy.

to move people from a dangerous place
The police ordered everyone to evacuate the building immediately.

to make an urgent, emotional request
He decided to plead guilty to the charges.

to cause (something) to become thoroughly soaked with liquid or moisture
The heavy rain will saturate the soil.

Provide (a house or room) with furniture; supply with something.
They plan to furnish the new apartment next month.

to come between so as to prevent or alter a result or course of events
The police had to intervene to stop the fight.

to lessen the effectiveness, power, or ability of, especially gradually or insidiously
His constant criticism began to undermine her confidence.

resist, endure
The old bridge was built to withstand strong winds.

to make familiar with
It took time to accustom myself to the new climate.

to provide food or services
The restaurant can cater for large parties.

to expel from a country
The government decided to deport the undocumented immigrants.

to hit sharply
She smacked the ball over the net.

to pursue stealthily; to walk stiffly
The lion stalked its prey.

admit that something is true or valid after first denying or resisting it
He had to concede that his opponent was right.

stop producing or providing something
The company decided to discontinue the product line.

pull or twist out of shape; give a misleading account of
The media can sometimes distort the truth.

to make as large or great as possible
We need to maximize our profits this quarter.

consider again, especially for a possible change of decision
Please reconsider your decision to leave.

stop oneself from doing something
Please refrain from talking during the movie.

produce a copy or something similar; produce offspring
These animals reproduce very quickly.

formally put an end to
The government plans to abolish the tax next year.

state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully
He asserted his innocence despite the evidence.

say or shout repeatedly in a rhythmic way
The crowd began to chant the team's name.

flatten by pressure; squeeze or press together
You can compress the file to save space on your hard drive.

recognize or ascertain what makes (someone or something) different
It's hard to differentiate between the two identical twins.

cause (someone) to lose confidence or enthusiasm
Don't let one failure discourage you from trying again.

to cause something unpleasant to be suffered
The storm inflicted severe damage on the town.

to cover (a road, path, etc.) with a hard, level surface
The workers will pave the new road next week.

to suppose that something is true without proof
I presume you're coming to the party tonight?

to organize something in a new way
The company decided to restructure its departments.

to exceed; to be greater than
His performance surpassed all expectations.

give official permission for or to
The manager will authorise the payment.

talk with excessive pride and self-satisfaction
He likes to boast about his achievements.

institute legal proceedings against (a person or organization)
The state decided to prosecute the suspect.

to underestimate the value or importance of
Don't underrate the importance of practice.

to achieve or reach (a goal, status, or level)
He worked hard to attain his goals.

prepare and use (land) for crops or gardening; try to acquire or develop (a quality, sentiment, or skill)
She tried to cultivate a more positive attitude.

to experience something unpleasant as a result of one's own actions
He incurred heavy losses in the stock market.

To accept or act in accordance with (a rule, decision, or recommendation)
You must abide by the rules of the game.

plan or invent (a complex procedure, system, or mechanism) by careful thought
They had to devise a new strategy to win the game.

interrupt (an event, activity, or process) by causing a disturbance or problem
The loud music began to disrupt the class.

give (someone) the authority or power to do something
Education can empower individuals to achieve their dreams.

to maintain or support (a custom, principle, or law)
It is important to uphold the law.

to lay down authoritatively; prescribe
The terms of the contract were dictated by the company.

to stick firmly to; to follow
Please adhere to the safety regulations.

to live in or at a specified place
He continues to dwell on his past mistakes.

to obstruct (someone or something) so as to prevent them from continuing to a destination
The police managed to intercept the package before it reached its destination.

to hit repeatedly with force
The strong winds began to batter the small boat.

to move continuously or freely through a closed system or area
The fan helps to circulate the air in the room.

to make something thoroughly clean
She used a special soap to cleanse her skin.

to feel a powerful desire for something
After a long day, I always crave a hot cup of tea.

to fall, drop, or hang loosely; to fail completely
The movie was a complete flop at the box office.

to shine with a sparkling light
The snow glittered in the sunlight.

to frighten or overawe someone
Don't let his size intimidate you; stand your ground.

to keep someone in hardship and subservience by unjust authority
The government was accused of trying to oppress its own people.

to make a surprise attack
The soldiers planned to ambush the enemy convoy.

to make or become unclear
The rain started to blur the view through the window.

to dance to pop or rock music
Let's boogie all night long!

subject to aggressive pressure or intimidation
It is illegal to harass someone at work.

to go into or through something
The roots of the tree can penetrate deep into the soil.

to prove more powerful or superior; to be widespread
Justice will eventually prevail.

to make an exact copy; to reproduce
Scientists are trying to replicate the experiment results.

to make a long, high-pitched cry or sound
The dog started to whine at the door.

to express clearly
He struggled to articulate his feelings.
